motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Shared easing for entrances and interactions.

motion.name: js-gate
motion.value: <html class="js"> set by an inline head script
motion.purpose: Entrance animations arm only when the class is present; the script removes it without IntersectionObserver or under reduced motion, so content shows at rest.

motion.name: logo-in
motion.purpose: Hero logo entrance, then float.

motion.name: float
motion.purpose: Hero logo; loops forever.

motion.name: title-in
motion.purpose: Hero title (0.15s delay) and section headlines on scroll (0.9s).

motion.name: rise
motion.value: 0.9s ease-out, fill-mode backwards; opacity 0, translate 0 36px -> rest; .is-in sets opacity 1
motion.purpose: Lede (0.45s), actions (0.6s), and data-rise blocks on scroll. Releases its transform after playing so hover and used-state lifts work.

motion.name: stagger
motion.purpose: Tickets and photo frames entering in sequence.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Photo frames wipe in from the left.

motion.name: scroll-observer
motion.purpose: Adds is-in to data-rise blocks; also triggers the board flip.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: Section title echo outlines; loops forever.

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Contact icons (0/120/240ms).

motion.name: pulse
motion.value: 2.2s ease-in-out, 4 iterations while visible; scale 1.08 at 50%
motion.purpose: Floating WhatsApp button; restarts each time it reappears.

motion.name: ripple
motion.value: 2.2s ease-out, 4 iterations while visible; opacity 0.55 -> 0, scale 1 -> 1.9
motion.purpose: Red ring emitted by the floating button.

motion.name: flap-flip
motion.value: 0.6s ease-out, rotateX(-90deg) -> 12deg -> 0, brightness 1.8 -> 1; delay rowIndex*70ms + tileIndex*35ms
motion.purpose: Hours board flips in once when it scrolls into view.

motion.name: ticket-lift
motion.value: translate 0 -4px, 0.45s ease-out; stub background to red-hover, 0.3s
motion.purpose: Ticket hover.

motion.name: ticket-tear
motion.value: .is-used: ticket translate 0 -6px; stub translate(10px, 4px) rotate(7deg) from 0 100%, 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); body inset 2px #ef4136
motion.purpose: Used ticket ("bilhete usado") after tapping a service; lasts until reload.

motion.name: button-lift
motion.purpose: Button hover; active snaps back in 0.08s.

motion.name: topbar-hide
motion.purpose: Topbar slides away on scroll down past 120px, returns on scroll up.

motion.name: menu-wipe
motion.purpose: Mobile nav panel reveals top-down.

motion.name: review-pin
motion.value: .reviews.is-pinned: height 250vh, padding 0; .reviews__pin sticky top 0, min-height 100vh, centred, 1.25rem block padding
motion.purpose: Applied when width > 760 and content height + 40 <= viewport; recomputed on load, resize and fonts ready.

motion.name: review-scrub-pinned
motion.value: t = p * (n + 0.6) - i, p = scroll progress across section height - viewport
motion.purpose: Cards appear one by one; all are visible before the section unpins.

motion.name: review-scrub-free
motion.purpose: Phones and short screens: each card follows its own position.

motion.name: review-ease
motion.value: clamp(t, 0, 1), ease-out cubic 1 - (1 - t)^3; opacity 0 -> 1, translateY 34px -> 0, scale 0.97 -> 1
motion.purpose: Shared mapping for both review modes; reversible with scroll.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animations (including pseudo-elements) set to none, transitions 0.01ms, smooth scroll off, data-rise forced visible; JS skips the observer and the flip. Review cards are forced visible and the pin script does not run.

narrative.overview:
The page is a station hall after dark. It has one blue-black ground in two depths, edged with hairlines, and the logo's red used only where a signal is needed. The structure and restraint follow the owner's current reference, barbeariaabanca.com.br: a single dark ground, colour only as an accent, thin lines, and a pinned scroll that reveals the reviews one by one. The name's "Estação" (station) survives in the departure board, where each opening-hours character sits on its own split-flap tile.

Density is low and the tone is calm and confident. Sections alternate between Night Navy and Navy Deep, and each one opens on a 1px white hairline at 7%. Headlines are set large in Teko 600, in uppercase, and each section headline carries a faint outlined copy of itself behind it. Body copy is a wide grotesk in muted tints of the ground. Red marks what to act on or notice: the booking buttons, the ticket stubs, the stars, the hero's lead line, and the board's "today" and "closed" states. Depth is quiet. Tickets, review cards, the board, and the map sit on long, soft drops.

Motion is light. The logo spins in and then floats, headlines rise with a slight zoom while their echoes breathe, blocks and tickets rise as they scroll into view, a used ticket tears its stub loose, the reviews hold still while their cards appear one by one, and the hours board flips. Only the logo float and the echo breathe loop forever; everything else plays and stops. All entrance motion is opt-in through JavaScript, and every animation stops under reduced motion.

The system is honest about missing data. Any fact the owner has not supplied yet is shown inside a dashed outline, and only placeholders are dashed.
keyCharacteristics: One dark ground in two depths (navy and navy-deep) alternating by section, separated by 1px hairlines at 7% white.
Red is a signal, never a field: buttons, ticket stubs, stars, the hero lead line, and board states.
Teko 600 for display text, always uppercase. Archivo widened for body (wdth 112), nav, and buttons (wdth 125), and narrowed only for flaps (wdth 70).
Section headlines carry an outlined echo of themselves, set up and to the right.
Services as station tickets: a navy body and a red price stub, split by a dotted perforation with two semicircular bites.
Review cards in navy-deep with an inner dotted stitch and a soft drop, revealed one by one as the pinned section scrolls.
Split-flap tiles for times, which flip in once when the board scrolls into view.
Dashed lines mean a placeholder, which is data.

rules.name: The Photo Atmosphere Rule
rules.body:
Two sections carry a photograph behind their content, and both share one treatment so they read as a pair: a deliberate blur (`--photo-blur: 7px`, image scaled 1.08 to hide the blurred edge) under one veil (`--photo-veil: rgb(4 6 15 / 0.86)`, Navy Ink at 86%). The photo is atmosphere only, a field of colour and light, never read as content; the strong blur is intentional and also hides the low resolution of the owner's source images.
- **Hero:** the owner's facade photo (`assets/fachada.webp`, object-fit cover, positioned 48% 45%), under the shared blur and veil (`.hero::before`), plus a gradient that fades the bottom 45% into Night Navy. The logo seal in the hero is the one logo the visitor reads.
- **Reviews:** the owner's Instagram photo of a client drinking a beer during his cut (`assets/avaliacoes-fundo.webp`, upscaled to 1920² with Lanczos from the 1080² Instagram source and saved at WebP 92 to avoid a second round of artifacts; lazy-loaded, empty alt), placed as `.reviews__bg` inside `.reviews__pin`: object-fit cover, positioned 50% 40%, under the shared blur and a flat shared veil (`.reviews__pin::before`); the section ends on straight edges like every other section, with no fades (the owner rejected them). Replace the photo with the owner's original file when it arrives. Because the photo lives inside the sticky pin, it stays still while the cards reveal.
- **Layers:** in both sections, photo (z 0), veil (z 1), content (z 2).

rules.name: The One Logo Rule
rules.body:
Only one logo is visible at a time. While the hero logo is below the topbar, the topbar brand is hidden (`.topbar.logo-hidden`, opacity 0 and visibility hidden, 0.35s); it fades in once the hero logo scrolls under the bar.
- **Barber Red** (red): Sampled from the logo. It fills every booking button, the ticket stubs, the floating WhatsApp button, the contact icon discs, and the "Hoje" tag, tints the "today" row (22%), and draws the nav underline, the mobile menu's bottom edge, and the selection highlight.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: Every section is a navy depth, alternating Night Navy and Navy Deep, with a 1px hairline (rgb(255 255 255 / 0.07)) on its top edge. No section is filled with red or any light colour.

rules.name: The Red Is Signal Rule
rules.body: Red marks only what to act on or notice: buttons, ticket stubs, stars, ticket icons, the hero lead line, contact discs, and board states. Use Barber Red for fills and Signal Red for small marks and type on navy.

rules.name: The Amber Is Signage Rule
rules.body: Departure Amber belongs to the departure board alone, on its column heads. It is never a general accent.

rules.name: The Teko Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Every display use is Teko at weight 600: headlines, the hero lead line, ticket names, prices, the rating, review author names, and day names. Words in Teko are set uppercase. Teko is never used for running text; that is Archivo's job.

rules.name: The Wide Text Rule
rules.body: Archivo runs wide: wdth 112 for text, 125 for nav and buttons. Only the flaps go narrow (wdth 70), and only phone buttons step back to 100.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Prices and times use tabular figures so columns hold still.

rules.name: The Tone Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces by a ground step or a hairline first. Shadows lift only the tickets, the review cards, the board, the map, and the red buttons.

rules.name: The Night Map Rule
rules.body: The Google map embed cannot be styled, so it runs in night mode through a CSS filter on the iframe: `invert(0.9) hue-rotate(180deg) saturate(0.85) brightness(0.95) contrast(0.95)`. The light map turns dark, and the hue rotation brings the red pin and coloured icons back near their own colours. A page-blue tint was tried and dropped by the owner, because it muted the red pin.

rules.name: The Dashed Is Placeholder Rule
rules.body: Dashed borders are reserved for missing owner data: the `.tbd` inline outline and the empty photo frame. When data arrives, the dash is removed (the script drops `.tbd`; a filled frame loses its border). Dotted lines are decoration only: the inset stitches and the ticket perforation.

dos: Do alternate sections between Night Navy and Navy Deep, and open each one on the 1px hairline at 7% white.
Do keep any background photo as atmosphere: blurred 2–3px, under an 82% veil, behind the content layer.
Do keep red to signals: buttons, ticket stubs, stars, contact discs, and board states. Use Signal Red for small marks and type on navy.
Do use the red pill for every booking action, and the ghost pill only for a secondary action beside it.
Do set every display use in Teko 600, with words in uppercase.
Do echo each section h2 with `data-echo`, keeping the echo text identical and hidden from assistive tech.
Do pin the reviews only when the whole section fits the viewport, and make sure every card is fully shown before the section unpins.
Do mark any fact the owner has not supplied with the dashed placeholder, and remove the dash when the real value lands.

Do present services as station tickets: the name and duration on the navy body, the price and booking cue on the red stub, and the whole ticket as one link. A used ticket says "BILHETE USADO", never "agendado".
Do set times and prices in tabular figures. Times go on split-flap tiles.
Do keep tap targets at least 44px tall.
Do keep entrance motion behind the `js` gate, loop only the logo float and the echo breathe, and stop all animation under reduced motion.
donts: Don't fill a section with red or any light colour.
Don't use dashed borders for anything except missing data.
Don't use Departure Amber outside the hours board.
Don't set Teko in lowercase, at another weight, or for running text, and don't add a faux-bold stroke.
Don't put small labels or kickers above section headlines. The red lead line exists only as the first clause of the hero h1, and the ticket number exists only as the ticket's own serial line.
Don't add hard offset shadows or glows. Depth is a ground step, a hairline, or a long, soft drop; the only rings are the floating button's white ring and the used ticket's inset Signal Red ring.
